subject: experian

error_analyses.pattern_hypothesis: Inline recovery link jumps past core form controls
error_analyses.observable_characteristics: The source is the 'Forgot username link' placed beside or near the username field in the sign-in form. The destination is the 'Learn more about our services link' below the sign-in card. In navigation_order, this moves from meaningful position 3 to position 6, while labels move from 5 to 6. The screenshots show additional form content between these areas, including the password field, sign-in button, and a remember-username checkbox region. The KFG also contains intermediate focusable controls after the forgot-username link, including the password input, a forgot-password link, a checkbox, and the sign-in button.
error_analyses.matching_criteria: A transition starts from an auxiliary link embedded within a form section and moves to a lower-page promotional or secondary link, while the implemented focus sequence omits one or more still-visible, functionally central controls in the same form that are present elsewhere in the KFG.
error_analyses.possible_cause: Observed: the detector did not report this ground-truth LNF even though the KFG shows a direct TAB edge from the forgot-username link to the lower 'Learn more' link. Hypothesis: the detector may have underweighted this transition because the implemented labels are consecutive (5 to 6), even though the meaningful positions show a larger jump across the sign-in workflow, or because it treated the destination as a nearby continuation rather than a form-disrupting jump.
error_analyses.supporting_evidence: Ground truth includes this exact transition. evaluated_transitions marks it FN and observed_in_stage1=True. navigation_order lists '/form[1]/div[2]/a[1]' as position 3 label 5 and '/app-signin[1]/div[1]/div[1]/a[1]' as position 6 label 6. KFG edges include TAB from '/form[1]/div[2]/a[1]' to '/app-signin[1]/div[1]/div[1]/a[1]'. KFG also lists password input, forgot-password link, checkbox, and sign-in button as focusable nodes between the form area and the lower link.

error_analyses.pattern_hypothesis: Cyclic wrap-around mistaken for linear-navigation failure
error_analyses.observable_characteristics: The source is the 'Sign In button' in the main form and the destination is the 'Experian logo link in header'. In navigation_order, this is from meaningful position 5 back to position 1, with implemented labels 3 to 4. The KFG shows a direct TAB edge from the sign-in button to the header logo, indicating a forward wrap to an earlier page element. The screenshots show later page elements still exist below the form, including the 'Learn more about our services' link and footer links, so the transition is visually non-local and not simply the end of all page content.
error_analyses.matching_criteria: A transition goes by TAB from a lower or mid-page control back to an earlier header element, producing a cyclical focus path, but the reference data does not label that wrap transition itself as an LNF.
error_analyses.possible_cause: Observed: the original detector reported this transition, but it is not in ground_truth. Hypothesis: the detector likely treated any TAB movement to a much earlier meaningful position as an LNF, without modeling that this page's reference labeling instead places the main problems on earlier intra-form jumps and the header-to-form jump rather than on the later cycle-closing edge.
error_analyses.supporting_evidence: original_predictions contains this exact transition. evaluated_transitions marks it FP and observed_in_stage1=True. navigation_order maps the sign-in button to position 5 label 3 and the header logo to position 1 label 4. KFG edges include TAB from '/form[1]/div[5]/button[1]' to '/ecs-header[1]/div[1]/div[1]/div[1]/div[1]/a[1]'. Ground truth lists other transitions but not this one.

error_analyses.pattern_hypothesis: Field-to-field jump hides intervening helper link
error_analyses.observable_characteristics: The transition goes from the 'Username input' directly to the 'Password input'. In navigation_order, this skips meaningful position 3 ('Forgot username link') and moves from position 2 to 4, while labels are consecutive from 1 to 2. The screenshots place the forgot-username link adjacent to the username area and above the password area. The KFG confirms a direct TAB edge from the username input to the password input even though the forgot-username link is also a focusable node elsewhere in the graph.
error_analyses.matching_criteria: A transition moves directly between two major form fields in consecutive implemented focus order, while an intervening focusable helper/recovery link exists in the same visible form region and is assigned an intermediate meaningful position.
error_analyses.possible_cause: Observed: the detector missed a ground-truth LNF that has consecutive implemented labels. Hypothesis: the detector may have assumed direct field-to-field movement is usually normal and therefore failed to flag this case because it looked semantically plausible, especially when relying on control-type continuity or adjacency rather than intermediate meaningful-position evidence.
error_analyses.supporting_evidence: Ground truth includes this exact transition and evaluated_transitions marks it FN. navigation_order shows username input at position 2 label 1, forgot username at position 3 label 5, and password input at position 4 label 2. KFG edges include TAB from username input directly to password input. The forgot-username link is present as a distinct node and is visible in screenshots near the username section.

error_analyses.pattern_hypothesis: Header entry lands on secondary link instead of first field
error_analyses.observable_characteristics: The source is the header logo link at the top of the page and the destination is the 'Forgot username link' within the sign-in card. In navigation_order, this moves from meaningful position 1 to 3, bypassing position 2 ('Username input'), while labels move from 4 to 5. The KFG shows a direct TAB edge from the header logo to the forgot-username link. Screenshots show the username field is visually the first main control in the sign-in form under the header.
error_analyses.matching_criteria: A transition begins in a top-level header/navigation element and lands on a secondary in-form link, while a primary field or action in the target content area is visible and given an earlier meaningful position.
error_analyses.possible_cause: Observed: the detector did not report this ground-truth transition despite a direct KFG edge. Hypothesis: it may have treated the move as acceptable because the source and destination are both links or because the destination remained within the same broad sign-in region, causing the skipped primary field to be overlooked.
error_analyses.supporting_evidence: Ground truth and evaluated_transitions both identify this exact transition as an FN. navigation_order lists the header logo as position 1 label 4, the username input as position 2 label 1, and forgot username as position 3 label 5. KFG edges include TAB from the header logo to '/form[1]/div[2]/a[1]'. The screenshots show the username input above the forgot-username link within the card.

correct_transition_examples.relevant_characteristic: Useful contrast with the FN from forgot-username to learn-more: this lower-page transition follows both implemented and meaningful order consecutively and does not jump back into the form.
Provides comparison for field/action movement that the reference does not label as LNF, despite omitted checkbox and forgot-password controls in the KFG candidate set.
Shows a normal consecutive transition within a visually grouped footer cluster, useful contrast against the FP wrap-around jump to the header.

subject_summary: This subject shows a sign-in page where implemented focus order diverges from the page's apparent form structure, especially around helper links embedded in or near the username/password areas. The false negatives mostly involve the detector missing jumps that land on or depart from secondary links while bypassing primary form controls, often because implemented labels remain consecutive or elements share similar link/form context. The single false positive appears to be a wrap-around TAB edge from the sign-in button back to the header logo that the detector treated as an LNF, although the reference data does not. Some uncertainty remains because the reference labels do not always align with every visually unusual KFG edge, so error causes are partly inferential rather than directly established.
